_meta.description: Document-rules config for legal_notice_defamation — pre-litigation notice for defamation (civil tort or criminal under BNS 356)
_meta.change_protocol: All edits require CLO sign-off. Defamation pleadings are high-risk — advocate must verify facts of publication, identification, and harm before issue.

partyDesignations.label: Noticee / Maker / Publisher of Defamatory Imputation

route.note: Civil = tortious defamation. Criminal = BNS Section 356.

mandatoryClauses.name: Publication to a Third Party
mandatoryClauses.description: Defamatory statement was made/published to at least one person other than the aggrieved (essential element)

mandatoryClauses.name: Identification of Aggrieved
mandatoryClauses.description: Aggrieved was identified or identifiable by reasonable readers/listeners

mandatoryClauses.name: Defamatory Imputation
mandatoryClauses.description: Reproduce the exact defamatory words or imputation verbatim; explain innuendo if not facially defamatory

mandatoryClauses.name: Falsity / Lack of Justification
mandatoryClauses.description: Assert that imputation is false and not protected by truth, fair comment, or privilege

mandatoryClauses.name: Damage to Reputation
mandatoryClauses.description: State the nature of harm — reputational, social, business, mental anguish

mandatoryClauses.name: Demand for Apology / Retraction / Takedown
mandatoryClauses.description: Specific demand for public apology, retraction, content removal, and damages

mandatoryClauses.name: Response Window
mandatoryClauses.description: Reasonable response window — typically 15 days; reservation of right to sue thereafter

mandatoryClauses.name: Advocate Details
mandatoryClauses.description: Name and BCI enrollment number of advocate

filingChecklist: Notice sent by Registered Post AD / Speed Post AD to each addressee
Where publication was online, also serve by email with delivery + read receipts
Postal receipts and AD card preserved
Screenshots / archive (archive.org) of defamatory content preserved with timestamps before issuing notice
Witness affidavits of third-party readers/viewers preserved (proof of publication)
Copy of notice with proof of service to be enclosed if civil suit / criminal complaint is later filed
Limitation: Civil suit under Article 75 Limitation Act = 1 year from publication; do not delay

sections.description: Defamation — definition, exceptions, and punishment (replaces IPC Sections 499–500)
Cognizance of offence — defamation triable on complaint of aggrieved
Tortious defamation — libel (written) and slander (spoken); remedies = damages + injunction
Suit for compensation for libel — 1 year from publication
Suit for compensation for slander — 1 year from words spoken
Intermediary liability — basis for takedown demand to platforms

validation_rules.description: Defamatory words must be reproduced verbatim; paraphrase is insufficient
At least one third-party recipient must be identified
Cooling-off window must be at least 15 days
No statutory pre-suit notice period; but reasonable opportunity required for good faith
Issue notice well within 1-year limitation under Article 75/76

promptInstructions: Draft a Legal Notice for Defamation. Route may be civil (tort), criminal (BNS Section 356), or both — confirm from input.
If criminal route, cite BNS Section 356 (not IPC 499/500 — IPC stands repealed for offences committed after 1 July 2024).
If civil route, base on tort of defamation — establish publication, identification, defamatory imputation, falsity, and damage.
Reproduce the exact defamatory words or imputation verbatim. If innuendo, explain the secondary meaning understood by audience.
State the date, medium (newspaper/social media/email/oral statement), and audience reach of publication.
Establish identification — that the aggrieved was named or reasonably identifiable.
Assert falsity and absence of any defence (truth, fair comment, privilege, public interest).
Quantify harm — reputational, social, business loss, mental agony.
Demand: (a) public apology, (b) retraction, (c) content takedown, (d) damages, (e) undertaking not to repeat.
Give a 15-day response window. State that failure will lead to civil suit and/or criminal complaint under BNS 356.
Reserve all rights — injunction, damages, criminal prosecution.
Do NOT generate the advocate signature block — it is added programmatically.
